findings.reason: I checked the matcher: `substring(3,5)` always returns 't' plus the first grant character (for example "ta"), which never equals a grant shortcut, and the condition is inverted, so it accepts any `xxxxxx:uuid` and none of the four event expectations actually checks the grant.
Line 73 does check `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId`, but every caller passes `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()`, so no real input reaches the null case.

I confirmed `ClientCredentialsGrantType` builds its token with `responseBuilder().generateAccessToken()` and never sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`; the only places that set it are ROPC, refresh, token exchange, pre-authorized code and `OAuth2GrantTypeBase`, so client-credentials tokens are encoded with 'na' instead of 'cc'.

The javadoc does say '3-letters' while the decoder requires exactly 2 characters, and there is no length or null check, so a custom grant that follows the doc would produce ids that cannot be decoded; this is a real but marginal contract and documentation issue.

I verified the test never calls `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null; looking up 'ac' falls into the refresh branch and throws an NPE, which the broad `RuntimeException` catch swallows, so the intended `IllegalArgumentException` path is never tested.
